name: tutorial-interactive
description: Plays the Tutorial Pit the way a first-time player does: every step is driven by a real click on the control the tutorial card points at — speed button, toolbar, hire buttons, blast panel, event choices — and each beat waits for the tutorial's own rails to advance (waitForTutorialStep) before the next click, mirroring the retired playtest definition's click path (seismic survey at 23,23; the box cut dug down the west face before the drill grid; drill grid on the exact 20,20-30,30 rectangle; haul before deliver). Every tutorial-facing step is role-marked 'player' or 'setup' (issue #479): a player step's interaction may not fall back to a console command, so a step that cannot actually be clicked fails the scenario instead of passing on a typed shortcut.

steps.description: Setup: load Tutorial Pit — the level regenerates the terrain at its own size and re-frames the camera. #553: cash bumped from $80,000 to $250,000 -- drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action, so this file needs a driving_center/training/drill_rig it never used to, on top of the original manager/driver/hauler/warehouse shopping list. #555: bumped again to $320,000 -- dig_ramp_segment is now gated the same way, so this file also needs a driving.excavator course and a rock_digger ($52,500 together) plus the extra payroll/fuel/maintenance drain of the real ticks box-cut now spends actually digging instead of completing in the same tick it was ordered.
Step time-speed: coach mark docked bottom-centre, speed button glowing, mine still visible

Command-mode-only unpause (issue #585): tutorial_start now genuinely sets isPaused (matches a real player's first view of the tutorial, paused so the card can be read) -- and tickCommand's own loop stops after exactly one real tick while paused regardless of the requested count, so every bare `tick N` below (training waits, haul waits) would silently advance only 1 tick without this. Interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep steps drive their own real clock independent of console pause state, so this resume has no effect there.
time-speed complete: real click on the speed button cycles 1x to 2x, card advances to Hire Surveyor
Player follows the glowing Crew button — the tutorial card must not swallow the click
hire-surveyor complete: Hire clicked in the crew panel, surveyor appears on site

expect.note: The tutorial is on rails: leaving for the world map mid-step is how a player loses it, so that button must be inert while the tutorial is up (mirrors tutorial.json's hire-surveyor beat).

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage: hiring already grants Rookie geology (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts, same for the UI hire button and this console command), so this only raises the level for tighter survey estimates. No role tag — there is no UI control for this and none should exist; the player-facing way to raise a skill is `employee train` at a training building, which this scenario does not need. Command mode keeps running it unchanged; interaction mode keeps it as an unmarked (legacy) command step.

the hired surveyor can actually be sent to survey: opening the Survey panel alone must already show a usable Run button — a surveyor who cannot survey is not a surveyor. If Run is disabled here, hiring grants no geology qualification and no button in the game grants one (mirrors tutorial.json's own standalone beat).

survey complete: seismic (the method the card names), target picked inside the step's outlined region (18..28), dispatched, and the surveyor walks out and works it. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock for the walk — no scripted `tick` needed once a click starts it.
hire-driller complete: driller hired through the crew panel

#681: build-living-quarters complete -- the tutorial's new step 3a-i, placed right after hiring the driller and before the box-cut/drill-plan/charge/sequence stretch that used to run this crew unmanaged for ~400 ticks. A tier-1 living_quarters gives that stretch's forced rest somewhere real to send a collapsing employee.

#681: set-early-policy complete -- the tutorial's new step 3a-ii. A living_quarters alone does not force anyone to rest: forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy (GameLoop.ts) only engages once state.sitePolicy.revision > 0, so this policy application is what actually makes the building above protect the crew through the grind that follows. Selects Continuous under Shift Mode first, then Apply -- shift_8h's own SHIFT_DURATIONS_TICKS (8) is shorter than a single drill_hole action, so applying it this early interrupted the queued vehicle-gated work below before it could finish (confirmed live pre-#700). Continuous still forces rest on hunger/fatigue (shouldForceRest checks that in every mode), just without the shift-length cap. The later set-policy step (unchanged) still teaches shift_8h once the grind is over. #707: timeout 15 -> 30 -- this was the only step in the file below the 30s floor every other player step uses; its `waitForTutorialStep` action's own inner deadline defaults to 30000ms (interaction-executor.ts) but effectiveStepTimeoutMs (scenario-utils.ts) doesn't know that action's `timeout` field (only `timeoutMs`/its own DEFAULT_INNER_TIMEOUT_MS table), so the outer 15000ms raced and lost first on a slow (no-GPU, #475) render -- confirmed live: the tutorial card had already reached 'build-driving-center' by the time the step's own 15s wall clock expired.

#553: build-driving-center complete: driving_center built through the Build panel -- drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action (a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole), and hiring only grants the driller their 'blasting' qualification, never the driving.drill_rig licence a drill_rig needs. This step and the two after it (train-driller, buy-drill-rig-assign) close that gap, the same deadlock class #552 fixed for hauling.

#553: train-driller, click half: driving.drill_rig course booked at the driving_center just built. Training itself takes real ticks (TRAINING_BASE_TICKS, balance.ts) -- command mode has no implicit clock between steps (unlike interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep), so the wait is its own step right below, mirroring this file's existing tick-1/tick-6 wait-only beats.

#553: train-driller complete: the training course finishes and the driller (employee #2) is granted driving.drill_rig. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick since it has no implicit clock between steps.
buy-drill-rig-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 drill_rig bought and placed on the terrain surface

#553: buy-drill-rig-assign complete: Assign clicked, then the tutorial's own clock runs while the newly-licensed driller (employee #2) walks to the drill_rig and boards -- the drill-plan step right after this one can only ever land a hole once this actually completes.

#555: train-digger, click half: driving.excavator course booked at the driving_center built above -- dig_ramp_segment work (the box-cut step below) now requires this licence + a rock_digger vehicle, the same gate #553 put on drilling. The surveyor (employee #1) is idle since the survey step completed, so they're who trains here. Training itself takes real ticks (TRAINING_BASE_TICKS, balance.ts) -- command mode has no implicit clock between steps, so the wait is its own step right below, mirroring train-driller's own click/wait split above.

#555: train-digger complete: the training course finishes and the surveyor (employee #1) is granted driving.excavator. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick since it has no implicit clock between steps.
buy-rock-digger-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 rock_digger bought and placed on the terrain surface

#555: buy-rock-digger-assign complete: Assign clicked, then the tutorial's own clock runs while the newly-licensed digger (employee #1) walks to the rock_digger and boards -- box-cut's own dig_ramp_segment work can only ever land a segment once this actually completes.

box-cut complete: dig the starter cut down the west face of the drill pattern before the first shot, so the blasted rock has a free face and a void to fall into (real open pits pioneer this access cut first). waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock — no scripted `tick` needed.

expect.note: Open pits start with an access cut dug before the first shot: blasted rock swells and needs a void to fall into (mirrors tutorial.json's box-cut beat).

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage — see the geology assign_skill step above for why this stays an unmarked (legacy) command step in interaction mode too.

#707: test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage — grants employee #1 (surveyor→digger, trained driving.excavator above) the blasting qualification. `charge_hole` gates on `requiredSkill: 'blasting'` alone (mining.ts) -- no vehicle or driving licence needed -- so employee #1, idle since box-cut finished, can now split the 9 `charge_hole` dispatches with the driller (employee #2) instead of the driller carrying drilling and all 9 charges alone. That single-employee grind is what let interaction mode's extra polling ticks (interaction-mode ticks run further ahead than command-mode ticks for the same step sequence) push well-being to 0 and hold it past REVOLT_TICKS (120 ticks, balance.ts), ending the level in a genuine worker_revolt moments before the blast step. Splitting the charge workload across two qualified employees shortens the real-tick span charging takes, closing that race. See the geology assign_skill step above for why this stays an unmarked (legacy) command step in interaction mode too.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: drill-plan, click half: grid tool dragged over the exact 20,20-26,26 rectangle the card asks for, confirmed. #553: this only orders the 9 holes -- drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action, so holeCount stays 0 until the driller (equipped above) actually drives the drill_rig to each one. The wait is its own step right below. #554-followup (issue #586 CI, rounds 4-5): round 4 corrected the command from rows:3 cols:3 spacing:5 (9 holes) to rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 (16 holes), reasoning the spacing stepper is unreachable this early in the rail (confirmed live, still true) so the declared spacing:5 could never be real. That was half right: spacing really is stuck at the tool's own DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3, but the drag rectangle producing 16 holes at that spacing was itself a latent bug in the region the tutorial rail snaps this drag to (REGION.drill, tutorialStages.ts), sized for a spacing of 5 that Drill.ts has never actually used since #479 -- nothing caught it because charging was instant until #553/#554, so the extra holes never cost real time. Round 5 fixes REGION.drill directly (20-30 -> 20-26), restoring the tutorial's originally-intended 3x3/9-hole workload for a lone early-tutorial employee with no living quarters yet; a 16-hole grid drove that same employee into a full worker revolt partway through charging (see the charging step's own note below). Command and drag corrected back in step to match the fixed region.

#553: drill-plan complete: the driller drives the drill_rig to all 9 ordered holes and drills them (sandbox-measured: a single driller/drill_rig lands a 3x3 spacing:3 grid on tutorial_pit comfortably inside 400 ticks door-to-door). #554-followup round 6 (issue #586 CI): previously used waitForTutorialStep(stepId:'charge'), which resolves the instant the FIRST hole lands (createComparisonStep's isComplete fires on the first increase past its snapshot -- 'drill-plan' advances to 'charge' after hole 1 of 9, not all 9). The very next step's `charge hole:*` order then only covered whatever was drilled AT THAT MOMENT -- usually just the one hole -- leaving the other 8 permanently uncharged (no later step re-issues the order), which is what left 'Auto Sequence' unreachable further down: charging never actually finished. Switched to waitUntil on holeCount itself so this step keeps waiting until every hole is actually down, in both modes, rather than stopping the moment the tutorial card first flips.

Defensive: a `tick N` step silently completes fewer ticks than requested if a random event fires mid-wait, and every subsequent tick then refuses until the event is resolved. No-op when nothing is pending.

charge ordered: Charge All Holes clicked — the panel applies its own form defaults and hole rows turn amber/loading (#554: charging is real work now, so the click only queues the order; the wait step right after drains it and confirms the tutorial advances to sequence once every hole has actually landed).

#554-followup round 6 (issue #586 CI): earlier rounds waited only for the FIRST charge to land (tutorialStep flips to 'sequence' the instant chargedCount first increases -- createComparisonStep's isComplete, same premature-advance behaviour as drill-plan above) and moved on with 8 of 9 holes still uncharged. That left 'Auto Sequence' unreachable further down the file: the sequence panel's own auto-sequence control only ever became reachable once every ordered charge had actually landed, so a scenario that stopped at chargedCount:1 could never proceed no matter how the following steps were reshuffled. Waiting for full completion here (chargedCount:9) is the real fix -- the drill-plan step above now also waits for all 9 holes before charging is ordered (round 6), so this order only ever targets the full 9 in the first place, unlike the partial orders earlier rounds were chasing. A 16-hole grid at this same lone-employee, no-living-quarters stage drove a full WORKER REVOLT at cumulative tick 318 (WorkerRevolt.ts's REVOLT_TICKS=120 sticky-zero window); REGION.drill (tutorialStages.ts) was fixed at the source to restore the tutorial's originally-intended 3x3/9-hole workload, which comfortably finishes charging well short of that threshold.
sequence complete: Auto Sequence clicked, delay labels appear on every hole
blast complete: Execute clicked, confirm dialog answered, crater and fragments appear, Blast Report closed; the scores card then auto-advances into the scripted consultant event

expect.note: Close dismisses BlastReportModal, which auto-opens with the real report right after DETONATE; scores card auto-advances, so tutorialStep is checked in the next beat (mirrors tutorial.json's own choice not to assert it here). holeCount/chargedCount/sequencedCount resetting to 0 is checkable in both modes and goes beyond what the DOM-only playtest reference could prove.

steps.description: event-fire-resolve complete: the consultant dialog is answered through its own buttons, outcome read, then dismissed

hire-manager complete: manager hired now that the event is resolved. #776: raised from 30s to 60s -- this step lands right after the blast sequence (steps 24-31) when the scene is heaviest, and effectiveStepTimeoutMs's formula-correct 35000ms (30s declared vs innerMs+margin) proved empirically insufficient in two independent interaction-mode runs, both timing out at exactly 35000ms with the real hire + tutorial advance to contract-accept already having succeeded before the deadline fired.

#689-followup: the build-living-quarters relocation (13,4 -> 18,14, this file's own earlier steps) shortens the crew's commute enough to clear the drilling deadlock, but it also shifts every tick landing downstream of it -- this step now lands at tick 340 instead of the pre-relocation value, and the contract offer pool (REFRESH_INTERVAL=20 ticks, Contract.ts) doesn't happen to carry a rubble_disposal offer at that exact tick (8 ore_sale offers, no rubble_disposal, direct trace). rubble_disposal is the one contract type this file can actually deliver later (consumeStoredOre() draws on raw storedMassKg, which the debris hauler fills; ore_sale/supply need specific ore this hauler never produces) -- not a type this step can simply switch away from the way level2-playthrough-win.json's own accept steps do. #707: retargeted 400 -> 300 -- granting employee #1 blasting (new bootstrap step above, before drill_plan) lets them share the 9 charge_hole dispatches with the driller instead of the driller carrying all 9 alone, so charging now finishes by tick 288 (command mode) instead of ~340, and this step's own entry tick drops with it. Direct trace (command mode) confirms the pool carries a rubble_disposal offer continuously from tick 289 through tick 339 (8-offer pool, one rubble_disposal slot, evicted at 340) -- 300 sits well inside that window with margin on both sides, still deterministic given the fixed seed. No state-dump field for 'a rubble_disposal offer exists' to wait on directly, same as before. #707 follow-up (this fix): the real root cause of #707's worker_revolt was `forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy` (GameLoop.ts) silently skipping idle employees, leaving them to the much-lower reactive NEED_WARNING_THRESHOLDS instead of the site policy's own proactive thresholds -- fixed in core, not this file. That core fix makes idle employees rest proactively more often, which costs a few extra real ticks: this step's own entry tick moves from 288 to 303 (command mode, direct trace). The contract offer pool's rubble_disposal window shifts with it, now continuous from tick 304 through tick 339 (evicted at 340, same 20-tick refresh cadence) -- retargeted 300 -> 320 to keep comfortable margin on both sides of the new window (16 ticks above the floor, 19 below the eviction) instead of sitting right at its old edge. #707 follow-up 2 (this fix): a live interaction-mode run of the whole file got past the blast steps (25-33) cleanly but stalled here -- interaction mode's own extra role:'player' polling ticks (waitForTutorialStep/waitForSelector loops that command mode's plain `command` string never runs; see this rule doc's tick-divergence note) land it on this step at tickCount 370, already past 320 -- and `equals` only matches going forward, so the old target was permanently behind by the time interaction mode reached it. Command-mode direct trace of the pool from tick 340 onward (same seed, same deterministic generation -- whether tick T's pool carries a rubble_disposal offer is a pure function of T alone, per this rule doc) found the 289-339 window closes at 340 with no rubble_disposal offered again until tick 400, at which point one offer (id 26, qty 120kg, deadlineTicks 58) opens and then holds that exact same pool slot continuously through tick 559 before rotating to a new instance -- a much wider, single-instance window than the 304-339 one this step used to target. Retargeted 320 -> 420: comfortably inside the 400-559 window on both sides (20 ticks above the floor, well short of the next rotation), reachable from interaction mode's own tick-370 entry in 50 ticks and from command mode's tick-303 entry in 117 ticks -- both well under the widened max_ticks/timeoutMs budget below. maxTicks 90 -> 140 (needs to cover command mode's own larger 117-tick gap, not just interaction's 50) and timeoutMs 60000 -> 150000 to match (each `tick 1` here is one page.evaluate round trip, not a rendered frame -- no per-frame terrain cost, but budgeted generously since interaction-mode tick cost is unmeasured under CI load); outer `timeout` raised 60 -> 150 to stay >= timeoutMs/1000 (`interaction-actions.test.ts`'s own outer/inner regression check, not just effectiveStepTimeoutMs's runtime margin).

contract-accept complete: Accept clicked on the offer this step's `command` names. #513/#581: elsewhere in this file's sibling scenarios the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-type]`/`[data-contract-material]` rather than a bare `.bs-contract-accept` (which resolves to whichever offered card leads the DOM), so a scoped click can't silently accept a different contract than the command names. #653 review round (Finding 2): this step used to stay unscoped, reasoning that tutorialStages.ts's own 'contract-accept' stage declares its live target as the bare `#bs-contract-panel .bs-contract-accept` and that scoping raced the offer pool's own refresh clock (REFRESH_INTERVAL=20 ticks, Contract.ts) -- but an unscoped click accepts whichever offer leads the DOM, which is only rubble_disposal at some tick landings and a different type at others (replay-verified at varied timing), silently accepting the wrong contract while the later deliver step (scoped to `[data-contract-type="rubble_disposal"]`) then finds nothing to deliver and times out. Scoped now, matching contract-negotiation.json/contract-panel-visual.json's own accept steps: a `waitForSelector` on the scoped selector ahead of the click gives the refresh cycle time to surface the right card instead of assuming it's there instantly, and `expect.equals` on `activeContractCount` proves the right contract landed rather than merely some contract. #653: retargeted from `type:ore_sale material:gloomium` to `type:rubble_disposal` (no `material:` -- rubble_disposal contracts carry `materialId: ''`), because the ore_sale/gloomium contract this step used to accept could never actually be delivered later (see the deliver step's own note below) -- the debris hauler this tutorial buys only ever fills storage with excavation spoil, never an ore-bearing fragment. rubble_disposal is fulfilled by `consumeStoredOre()` drawing on raw `storedMassKg`, which the hauler does fill, making this the first contract type in this run the later deliver step can genuinely complete. Live-verified landing under real render load is ~100 extra ticks reaching this point (tick 332 vs command mode's tick 232), not the 300+ an earlier round of this file assumed. issue #585 (merge, agrees independently): a hardcoded id here is exactly as fragile as the DOM-scoped click above and for the same reason -- the contract pool's ids increment off total elapsed ticks (Contract.ts) -- reaching the same `type:rubble_disposal` selector via a separate trace before #653 landed. #776: raised from 30s to 60s -- this step lands right after the blast/event/hire-manager stretch above, and effectiveStepTimeoutMs's formula-correct ~35000ms (30s declared vs innerMs+margin) proved empirically insufficient in two independent interaction-mode runs, both timing out here with the real accept + tutorial advance to hire-driver already having succeeded before the deadline fired -- same shape as the hire-manager step's own #776 fix above.
hire-driver complete: driver hired through the crew panel

Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage — see the geology assign_skill step above; hiring already grants Rookie driving.truck, this only raises the level. Kept for command mode, which needs it for its own explicit `vehicle driver 1 4` to succeed identically.
vehicle-buy-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 hauler bought and placed on the terrain surface

vehicle-buy-assign complete: Assign clicked, then the tutorial's own clock runs while the driver walks to the vehicle and boards — the #478 deadlock path, exercised for real. #553: vehicle #2, not #1 -- the drill_rig bought earlier took vehicle slot #1 (destroyed by its own blast, but the id isn't reused). #653: vehicle #3, not #2 -- both vehicles bought earlier in this run (drill_rig #1, rock_digger #2) are destroyed by an earlier blast (vehicleCount 2→0, deathCount 0→2), so ids are never reused and the debris_hauler bought in the previous step is vehicle #3. issue #585 (merge, agrees independently): same #3 conclusion, confirmed via a separate direct trace before #653 landed.
build-storage complete: warehouse placed by clicking the step's outlined tile (6,6) in the Build panel picker

haul-debris complete (#552): automatic dispatch sends the hauler to a reachable fragment with no player click at all -- the retired Haul button is gone, so there is nothing left for this step to point at. The step teaches watching, not clicking: waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock for the haul exactly as before, just without a click triggering it. #653 follow-up: command mode's own `command` was widened from `tick 1` to `tick 20` -- verified live (command mode) that storedMassKg is still 0 at tick 10, first lands the hauler's full 1050kg load between tick 11 and tick 13 (walk-to-vehicle/board, drive-to-fragment, load, drive-back, unload all cost real simulated ticks that only started counting once this step's own ticks ran), and stays there afterward; tick 20 keeps ~7-9 ticks of margin over that observed landing point without approaching the accepted contract's 67-tick deadline. issue #585 (merge): the accept step above changed independently on both sides of the merge (scoped click instead of unscoped), shifting exactly when the hauler's dispatch clock starts counting relative to before #653's own 10/13/20-tick measurement; kept at 40 (this branch's own pre-merge value) rather than adopting #653's 20 outright, since a full command-mode replay of the merged file (all 43 steps) is a cheaper, equally valid check than re-deriving the exact new landing tick by hand -- confirmed clean end to end with 40, not re-verified at 20. #707: back down to 20 -- granting employee #1 blasting (new bootstrap step before drill_plan) shortens the charging phase enough that the wait_until step above now accepts the rubble_disposal contract at tick 300 instead of 400, and that specific pool instance's own deadlineTicks is 37, not the ~67 #653 measured against a different offer -- `tick 40` alone would cross tick 337 and expire the contract before delivery (direct trace, command mode); `tick 20` lands well inside the deadline while keeping #653's own measured hauler-load margin (loaded by tick 11-13 after dispatch).

expect.note: The old reported bug this beat guarded against (no UI control anywhere could trigger `vehicle haul`) no longer applies -- #552 retires the button and the whole manual flow, so there is nothing left to get stuck on. No increased check on storedMassKg here -- like hauling-gate.json (Finding #33), the exact delivered tonnage is position/timing-dependent, not the thing this beat proves.

steps.description: contract-deliver complete, now genuinely in both modes: Deliver clicked on the rubble_disposal contract accepted earlier; the finances card then auto-advances. #653: retargeted from `type:ore_sale material:gloomium amount:200` -- confirmed live that field-plan (even after fixing the vehicle-id step) leaves `collectedOre.gloomium` at 0kg for 600+ ticks, because the debris hauler only ever fills storage with excavation spoil (box-cut/ramp-carve debris), never an ore-bearing blast fragment, so that contract could never be fulfilled before its own deadline. rubble_disposal is fulfilled by `consumeStoredOre()` drawing on raw `storedMassKg` instead, which the hauler does fill. Interaction click scoped to `[data-contract-type="rubble_disposal"]` (unlike the accept step, which stays unscoped against the offer pool's own refresh race) -- safe here because `state.contracts.active` doesn't rotate the way the offer pool does: there is exactly one active contract at this point and no periodic refresh removing it. issue #585 (merge): kept amount:200 rather than #653's own exact-quantity 170 -- the merge shifts exactly which tick this contract is offered/accepted at (the accept step above now scopes its own click, and the haul-debris step above needed re-verifying against the combined file), so the contract's own exact remaining quantity is no longer pinned to the 170kg #653 measured against its own, pre-merge version of this file. amount:200 is a cap, not an exact figure -- it exceeds every rubble-disposal offer's own quantity seen in trace (120-170kg), so this caps at whatever the contract still needs and completes it outright regardless of the exact pool-dependent number, the same robustness #585's own original version of this step already had. Whether it reads COMPLETED or a partial "Delivered to" is pool-size-dependent and not asserted here. #707: amount:200 -> 300 -- granting employee #1 blasting shifted the accept step (see wait_until above) onto a different pool instance whose own quantityKg is 260, above the 120-170kg range #653/#585 traced; 200 alone left it short ("Delivered to", contract still active, activeContractCount stuck at 1). 300 restores the same cap-not-exact-figure margin over the new instance's own quantity, direct-traced (command mode) to complete outright. #707 follow-up 2 (this fix): the wait_until step above was retargeted from tick 320 to 420 for interaction mode's later arrival (see its own description) -- the pool instance offered at the new landing tick is a different one, id 26, quantityKg 120, direct-traced (command mode). amount:300 already exceeds that too, so it stays unchanged: still a cap, not an exact figure, still completes the contract outright regardless of which instance is in play.

expect.note: #653 follow-up: `equals` on `activeContractCount` (issue #653 review, Finding 1 -- scenario-defs.md forbids loosening this exact field to directional `increased`/`decreased`, since the number itself is the point) is checked in BOTH modes (checkGoalAgainstState, scenario-goal.ts) and now genuinely passes in command mode too, not just interaction mode -- widening the preceding haul-debris step's own tick budget (`tick 1` -> `tick 20`, see its own note) gives command mode's hauler real stock (storedMassKg 0 -> 1050kg) before this step's `contract deliver` command runs, so the delivery actually completes (`Contract #11 COMPLETED!`) and activeContractCount genuinely drops 1->0, instead of failing synchronously on "Not enough stored material" the way it silently did before this fix (the file's only prior check here, `tutorialStep`, is skipped in command mode entirely, so that failure never surfaced as a scenario failure). No `tutorialStep` assertion here (mirrors the blast step's own choice, line ~676): after delivery completes, the tutorial auto-advances through multiple sub-stages (finances -> needs -> set-policy) fast enough that which one is showing when this step's own check runs is a genuine race, not environmental flake -- an earlier round pinned it to "needs" and that intermittently failed once the auto-advance outran it. The interaction's own waitForTutorialStep still accepts any of finances/needs/set-policy so the click path keeps moving; the settled landing point is asserted downstream instead, at the set-policy step right after this one, once its own waitForTutorialStep(stepId:'tick-advance') has actually resolved (expect.tutorialStep:'tick-advance' there).

steps.description: set-policy complete: Apply pressed in the Operations panel (redesign P5 moved site policy out of Settings) — the form mirrors the policy in force, and applying it unchanged still counts

expect.note: Applies without touching a control first — the form mirrors the policy already in force, and it used to leave the step stuck while the panel said the policy had been updated (mirrors tutorial.json's own note).

steps.description: tick-advance complete: the tutorial's own clock runs — the whole point of this step — until tickCount has advanced more than 5, reaching the closing victory card. No click and no scripted `tick`: mirrors the retired playtest's own beat, which was `letTimePass` only.

expect.note: Either closing card is a correct outcome: victory hands off to the completion card as soon as the level's profit target is met, which is campaign economy rather than playability (mirrors tutorial.json's own note).

steps.description: victory complete: level ends, card shows Tutorial Complete. Forces the transition so the scenario ends deterministically rather than waiting out the profit-threshold win check; not a player action — `campaign` is on the reused setup allowlist.
Final: the congratulations card dismisses itself and the game is unpaused
